title: Mineral commodity summaries 2023
citation: U.S. Geological Survey, 2023, Mineral commodity summaries 2023: U.S. Geological Survey Mineral commodity summaries MCS-2023, map scale 1:148,000,000.
notes:
National mineral commodity statistics (front matter, summary tables and figures, and the Abrasives, Aluminum and Antimony chapters; pages 1-37, all pdf_text, no OCR needed; page 5 is absent from the packet, likely blank). No geologic map units, borings, wells, structures or aquifers are described, so no values were recorded. The only South Carolina content is the Table 3 row on page 15: South Carolina 2022 nonfuel mineral production value $1,160 million (partial total, footnote 7), rank 23, 1.18% of U.S. total; principal commodities cement, gold, sand and gravel (construction), sand and gravel (industrial), stone (crushed). These are economic statistics with no field in the extraction schema. No reference list on these pages.
Commodity chapters Arsenic through Chromium (pages 38-61, all pdf_text, no OCR needed). National and world production, trade and reserves statistics only; no geologic map units, borings, wells, structures, aquifers or South Carolina content, and no reference list. No values recorded.

National and world production, trade and reserves statistics only; no geologic map units, borings, wells, structures or aquifers, and no reference list. Commodity chapters Stone (crushed, continued) through Vanadium (pages 169-194, all pdf_text, no OCR needed). National and world production, trade and reserves statistics only; no geologic map units, borings, wells, structures, aquifers or South Carolina content, and no reference list. No values recorded.
Commodity chapters Vanadium (continued) through Zirconium and hafnium, and Appendices A-D (pages 195-214, all pdf_text, no OCR needed; page 211 has figure captions only). No geologic map units, borings, wells, structures, aquifers or reference list. South Carolina mentions, page 197 (Vermiculite): a company with operations in South Carolina did not expect to produce vermiculite in 2022; vermiculite occurrences in Colorado, Nevada, North Carolina, South Carolina, Texas, and Wyoming contain estimated resources of 2 million to 3 million tons. These are commodity resource statements with no field in the extraction schema, so not recorded. Whole document: a national commodity statistics volume with no extractable South Carolina geologic values; complete with no values.
